tweet.text:
I think there's a pretty high chance that Amazon eventually folds and lets agents run wild on their interface.

But they will need to have their advertising revenue offset to do that. Lots of ways this can happen, none mutually exclusive:

1. Agent pays to access the site
2. Agent pays a fee in form of small % of purchases made
3. Agents become a channel for ads, ad revenue gets shared with Amazon

All of these eventually get passed down to the user in some way.

This will be a bigger battle than anyone anticipates. It is only a matter of time before there is an Apple and Google version of Muse and possibly TikTok, in addition to the frontier LLM agents. Maybe a commerce agent from Amazon. 

Every app that is a services, marketplace or commerce app will need to existentially decide to open APIs for consumer agents to interact. Smaller players have no choice. Ad revenues are more than transaction fees, either the consumer benefits or distribution aggregators will demand a higher transaction fare. 

I know I don't want an agent for each app. I would like my agent to be able to do tasks I require. We can already see consumers getting trained on that behavior by the frontier labs.

tweet.text:
Tokenized equities have historically struggled with liquidity.

Onchain markets often struggle to adjust inventory as demand changes. Backpack lets any user create new token supply from equity positions held in its brokerage and redeem excess tokens back into brokerage positions. This allows liquidity to scale with demand instead of being limited by the tokens already in circulation.

This matters in DeFi because swaps and liquidations depend on liquidity already being available onchain. Backpack’s brokerage gives market makers a way to reliably provide inventory and quote onchain as demand changes. More reliable liquidity can improve execution and make tokenized stocks more practical as collateral.

Across several equities, Backpack delivered the lowest-cost round trip execution compared to other issuer versions.
